title: THR Hannibal — can Doubt preserve translation and attribution boundaries?
question: Does the bounded Human Record source path establish that Polybius' Greek text literally contains 'Hannibal' and that Sosylus was unreliable?
verdict: No. The checked Polybius surface is an English translation whose Greek literal was not inspected, and the negative judgement of Sosylus remains Polybius' reported evaluation rather than THR's adjudication.

nodes.label: Current position
nodes.text: The bounded record does not establish either stronger claim.

nodes.label: Translation boundary
nodes.text: The checked Polybius surface renders 'Hannibal' in English, while the Greek source literal was not inspected.

nodes.label: Attributed source criticism
nodes.text: The record preserves Polybius' criticism of Sosylus as Polybius' evaluation, not as THR's direct judgement.

nodes.label: Greek literal
nodes.text: The exact Greek source literal remains uninspected in the bounded record.

nodes.label: Independent reliability adjudication
nodes.text: The bounded sources do not independently adjudicate Sosylus' historical reliability.

edges.note: A checked English rendering does not establish the literal form of the uninspected Greek source text.
Attributing a negative judgement to Polybius prevents silently adopting that judgement as the project's own conclusion.
The missing Greek inspection blocks the literal-source claim.
The absence of an independent adjudication blocks the stronger reliability claim.
